# Additive tuning of 2026-10-31, base re-measure of scenario 1

## Run identity

```yaml
model: claude-sonnet-5
```

**This line is the `base` stage of round 1 of the engine layer, in the tuning round of the additive campaign that [#1877](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1877) asked for.** The plan on [#1877](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1877#issuecomment-6526205178) puts this stage first: it measures scenario 1, the documents alone, so that scenario 2, the documents and the engine, has a number to compare against. The owner accepted that plan [on the issue](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1877#issuecomment-6526210603), and [#1910](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/pull/1910) opened the layer at `d20eb3fd`. `tools/probe/try.sh launch` ran it from the one-line spec `additive scenario-1 tuning`. It is the `scenario-1` arm of the additive tier over the 22 probes of the tuning set, at 7 repetitions per probe, on `claude-sonnet-5` under Claude Code 2.1.288. The tool titled the line a re-measure, but it is the first measurement of scenario 1 at this count and pin.

**One tree, one pin, one launch.** Every session ran in a fresh copy of a `git archive` of the pinned tree, and the engine of that tree. The pin was `d20eb3fd` for the whole batch. The canary of 8 sessions held 4 records that named paths outside the workspace: each ran a `find /`-style search for an engine binary, a decision file or a crate cache, and the sandbox binds none of those paths. The owner read them and [passed the canary](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1877#issuecomment-6532986534) before `canary-passed` was written. The driver then halted six times, after a host credential refresh failed and during the owner's usage limit, and it continued in the same try root at the same pin. It did not launch the batch again. The `tree` digest in the identity above is the digest the assembly recorded.

**What the recorder counted.** The line holds 154 sessions and cost 11907 cents: the intent hook live in 0, 2 stopped at the turn cap, 1 stopped at the session budget, 133 paths outside the workspace named, 0 sessions uncounted, 0 web-tool calls. A session the recorder could not count adds nothing to either count, so each count is a floor.

**The result.** Scenario 1 passed 58 of the 153 sessions it graded. The base row compares this measurement with the screening measurement of scenario 1 on 2026-10-18, which passed 39 of 72 in [the screening transcript](additive-screening-of-2026-10-18-scenario-1.md). The difference is -16.3 points, with the interval [-29.5, -2.4]. The two measurements do not share a probe: the screening drew 4 probes of the old set, and [#1909](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/pull/1909) retired that set for the 22 frozen tuning probes that this line draws. So the row compares two different task sets, and it does not show that scenario 1 got worse. The keep rule does not read a base, and a base is never kept. `try.sh result` wrote `1 d20eb3fd` to the base pin, and a confirmation of the engine layer reads that pin.

**The contract of this batch.** The sessions ran under the recorder contract of spec 15: a `bwrap` sandbox with no network of its own, a configuration directory that holds a copy of the credentials and nothing else, the permission mode `dontAsk`, and `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` denied. The owner approved $1,300.00 for this layer, and `.headwater/probe.yml` holds $1,300.00 for the tuning round. The driver ran this try with a cap of 12000 cents and a session budget of 300 cents. At 141 of 154 sessions it stopped as capped, because retries that recorded nothing had used the cap, and the owner [raised the cap to 13500 cents](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1877#issuecomment-6536880201) for the last 13 sessions.

**What the batch cost.** The driver charged 12373 cents against its cap, and the 154 recorded sessions account for 11907 cents of that sum. Most of the difference is sessions that recorded nothing: three were cut off when a host credential refresh failed, and later attempts ran into the owner's usage limit. The 12373 cents go against the base ceiling of 25000 cents in `.headwater/probe.yml`, and not against the ceiling of 105000 cents for the tries. This line is the first charge to that base ceiling.

**Where the raw recordings are.** The raw session logs are outside git, under `/mnt/build/hw-1877/base-1/a/sessions/L1-*/raw.jsonl` on the host that ran the batch. Nobody deletes them until the report of [#1779](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1779) is published.

**Where the other figures are.** The rate and the interval of each probe are in the generated result that reads this transcript.

A block that holds no prose of this document's own author\\n/// pairs with an empty list.\\npub fn sentences_by_block(&self) -> Vec<(&Block, Vec<crate::sentences::Sentence>)> {\\n    self.blocks\\n        .iter()\\n        .map(|block| (block, crate::sentences::of_block(block, &self.links)))\\n        .collect()\\n}\\n```\\n\\nThen in `language.rs`'s `evaluate`, after/alongside the existing per-sentence loop, iterate `body.sentences_by_block()` (only over the actual body — not the `scent` front-matter facet, which has no block structure), filter to `is_running_prose(block.kind)`, and push a Warn finding when `sentences.len() > 6` (introduce a named constant alongside `MAX_WORDS`, e.g. `MAX_SENTENCES_PER_BLOCK: usize = 6`).\\n\\nThis repo has a strict convention (documented at length in the `DocumentCheck for Language` impl's doc comment on `const VERSION`) that ANY change to this rule's logic or message text must bump `const VERSION` and add a new `/// **Edition N, on <date>.** ...` paragraph explaining what changed and why a warm cache would otherwise serve a stale verdict — follow that convention for this change (current VERSION is 6; bump to 7; use today's date 2026-10-31; look at the existing edition paragraphs for the expected tone/structure, but keep your new one concise — a few sentences, not a replica of the longest ones).     - tool: "Bash"
```yaml
      argument: "{\"command\":\"python3 - <<'EOF'\\nimport re, glob, os\\n\\ndef paragraphs(text):\\n    # strip front matter\\n    if text.startswith('---'):\\n        parts = text.split('---', 2)\\n        if len(parts) >= 3:\\n            text = parts[2]\\n    # strip fenced code blocks\\n    text = re.sub(r'```.*?```', '', text, flags=re.S)\\n    lines = text.split('\\\\n')\\n    blocks = []\\n    cur = []\\n    for line in lines:\\n        if line.strip() == '':\\n            if cur:\\n                blocks.append(' '.join(cur))\\n                cur = []\\n            continue\\n        s = line.strip()\\n        # skip list items, headings, tables, blockquotes\\n        if re.match(r'^(#|[-*+]\\\\s|\\\\d+\\\\.\\\\s|\\\\||>)', s):\\n            if cur:\\n                blocks.append(' '.join(cur))\\n                cur = []\\n            continue\\n        cur.append(s)\\n    if cur:\\n        blocks.append(' '.join(cur))\\n    return blocks\\n\\ndef count_sentences(p):\\n    # approximate: split on ./?/! followed by space+capital, guard common abbreviations\\n    p = re.sub(r'\\\\b(e\\\\.g|i\\\\.e|etc|vs|U\\\\.S|U\\\\.K|a\\\\.m|p\\\\.m|Ph\\\\.D|U\\\\.S\\\\.C)\\\\.', lambda m: m.group(0).replace('.', '\\\\u0001'), p)\\n    parts = re.split(r'(?<=[.!?])\\\\s+(?=[A-Z0-9`\\\"‘“\\\\[])', p)\\n    parts = [x for x in parts if x.strip()]\\n    return len(parts)\\n\\ntotal = 0\\nover6 = 0\\nover8 = 0\\nfiles = glob.glob('docs/**/*.md', recursive=True)\\nfor f in files:\\n    try:\\n        text = open(f, encoding='utf-8').read()\\n    except Exception:\\n        continue\\n    for p in paragraphs(text):\\n        words = len(p.split())\\n        if words < 3:\\n            continue\\n        total += 1\\n        n = count_sentences(p)\\n        if n > 6:\\n            over6 += 1\\n        if n > 8:\\n            over8 += 1\\n\\nprint(\\\"files:\\\", len(files))\\nprint(\\\"paragraphs:\\\", total)\\nprint(\\\"over6:\\\", over6, \\\"over8:\\\", over8)\\nEOF\\n\"}"
      result: ""
    - tool: "Write"
```
